deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the motivation part of Grothendieck's 1967 lectures on crystals. On the previous page he notes that over C, an endomorphism f of X acts on the transcendental integral cohomology H^i(X,Z), so the characteristic polynomial of f^* on H^i is in Z[T] and independent of l. In characteristic p>0 there is no integral cohomology. The finiteness of H^i(X,Z_l) is known only for proper X or dim X <= 2.

This page continues that discussion. For X smooth projective over k of characteristic p, f^* acts on H^i(X,Q_l) for each l != p. The coefficients of det(1 - T f^* | H^i) therefore lie in Q_l. The first problem is whether they lie in Q and are independent of l. Grothendieck says that for X projective nonsingular one knows how to reduce this to a problem on algebraic cycles 'of Lefschetz type'. This is the germ of the standard conjectures, in particular conjecture B(X) (algebraicity of the Lambda operator) together with the conjecture comparing homological and numerical equivalence.

Then comes the 'paradox'. Suppose this 'concrete' rationality problem ('mod torsion') is solved affirmatively. Since f^* preserves the lattice H^i(X,Z_l)/torsion, each coefficient is l-integral for every l != p. But that only gives coefficients in Z[1/p], i.e. of the form n/p^s with n in Z, not integers. The defect comes from the restriction l != char k. It shows that a p-adic cohomology theory for varieties in characteristic p is missing.

The next page explains what such a theory should be: functors to finite Z_p- or Q_p-modules with Künneth, duality and the right Betti numbers. Serre's argument shows that no such Q_p-theory exists, already for H^1 (supersingular elliptic curves, whose endomorphism algebra is a quaternion algebra). The natural coefficient ring is W(k). This is the program realized by crystalline cohomology (Grothendieck, Berthelot), where f^* preserves H^i_cris(X/W)/torsion. That gives p-integrality and hence integrality, as obtained later via Katz–Messing for X over finite fields.
errors: No mathematical error. The step from 'rational and l-integral for all l != p' to Z[1/p] silently uses that f^* preserves a Z_l-lattice, namely H^i(X,Z_l) mod torsion, which is finitely generated for proper X. That is consistent with the previous page.

ideas.what: Rationality and l-independence of characteristic polynomials of endomorphisms on l-adic cohomology reduce to Lefschetz-type conjectures on algebraic cycles.
ideas.modern_name: Standard conjectures (Lefschetz-type B(X)); independence of l
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1968/69), Bombieri; results by Katz–Messing 1974 over finite fields
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968, publ. 1969)

ideas.what: Even granting rationality, l-adic theories (l != p) give only Z[1/p]-integrality; p-integrality requires a p-adic cohomology. This is the motivation for crystalline cohomology.
ideas.modern_name: Motivation for crystalline cohomology / p-integrality of characteristic polynomials
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968), introduction

deep.surprise_reason: Standard expository motivation for p-adic/crystalline cohomology, essentially as in Grothendieck's published IHES crystals notes and the standard conjectures paper. Nothing new.
